boundedScope: The thirteen supplied records in nine primary sources, plus the forest results required to make honest algorithm/lower-bound comparisons. No unbounded literature expansion.

representationDecision.userChoice: Both update time and number of recolored existing edges, in aligned panels
representationDecision.axes: Categorical cost-formula columns and common graph/palette/update rows. Column order is not a universal asymptotic ranking when Δ and ε vary.
representationDecision.semanticZoom: Detail 738×548 restores formula and cost-quantifier labels; compact 330×245 shows setup labels and markers; overview hides all text; focus uses the same chart.
representationDecision.color: Green algorithm circles/squares, red lower diamonds. Setup colors are restricted to row labels/brackets.
representationDecision.resources: No recourse bound is copied into update time. Recourse excludes the new edge's first color.

sources.evidence: Primary theorem text and Appendix A; independently audited by cc_lca
theorems: 2.1: Greedy O(1/(c+√Δ)) amortized for initially empty incremental forests, Δ≥3 and 0≤c≤Δ−2.
2.2: Matching lower only for a particular tie-breaking rule; kept related-only.
2.9: DistMaint Θ(1/Δ) expected amortized incremental recourse for all 0≤c≤Δ−2.
2.10: Universal Ω(1/Δ) expected amortized lower for fixed constant c, even randomized algorithms against oblivious adversary.
2.11: DistMaint Θ(min{Δ/c,log_(Δ+c−1)n}) expected per-update fully dynamic recourse. For c=0 interpret Δ/c as infinity; this is its own cost, not universal optimality at positive c.
2.12: Universal Ω(log_(Δ−1)n) amortized fully dynamic lower at c=0; randomized algorithms against oblivious adversary included.
2.13: Universal Ω(1) lower for fixed c; no parameter-dependent universal match asserted.
A.1: Fully dynamic implementation O(1+R) time for update recourse R.
A.2: Incremental implementation O(α_UF(n)+R) expected amortized time; union-find overhead prevents substituting O(1+R).
A.4: Greedy O(Δ⁴n) update time.
sources.machineModel: O(1) pointer/arithmetic and uniform integer sampling from ranges of size at most Δ+c, as stated in Appendix A.

theorems: 2.5: For integer 1≤C≤Δ−2 and C≥Δ/φ+0.724, O(m+Δ²) time and O(log n/[log((Δ+C)/(Δ−C))·(C/Δ−1/φ)]) recourse per insertion; fixed palette permits deletion without recoloring.

2.6: Ω(log(nC/(Δ−C)²)/log((Δ+C)/(Δ−C))) extension barrier for a specified partial coloring. Source warns it is not an amortized/expected dynamic lower and can be avoided by maintained invariants; related-only.
2.8: Sparse graph Δ-adaptive palette max{deg_t(u),deg_t(v)}+C, C≥(2+ε)α−1, O(m) worst-case time and O(ε⁻¹log n) worst-case recourse.
qualifiers: Dropping 1/(C/Δ−1/φ) requires constant separation from the threshold.
The paper's near-tightness comparison also needs Δ−C=O(n^(1−δ)).
α is a supplied upper bound for the sparse result, while current degree adapts.

theorems: Deterministic (2Δ−1)-edge coloring in O(log Δ) worst-case update time.
sources.correction: Removed the old numeric ratio-2 coordinate. No independent recourse formula inferred.
sources.limitation: Full proof theorem numbering was not required to state the published-abstract guarantee; record is explicitly primary_abstract_verified.

sources.evidence: Primary published abstract, with 2023 theorem discussion corroborating high-probability qualification
theorems: Near-(1+ε)Δ coloring in O(ε⁻⁴log⁸n) amortized update time for sufficiently large degree Δ≥Ω(ε⁻²log²n), ε a small constant.
sources.limitation: Primary abstract is the direct evidence; exact proof numbering/adversary strengthening not inferred.

theorems: O(ε⁻⁶log⁹n log⁶Δ) worst-case update time with high probability; fully dynamic, current-degree adaptive, without a high-degree promise.
§7.1 explicitly restores local palette ceilings ⌈(1+ε)d(v)⌉; global ⌈(1+ε)Δ⌉ follows.
sources.qualifier: Degree-adaptivity is not taken to mean adaptive-adversary robustness. No final coloring recourse formula inferred.

sources.evidence: Theorem 1.2, threshold before Theorem 1.1, Corollary C.6
theorems: O(log⁴(1/ε)/ε⁹) expected worst-case update time against an oblivious adversary with known sequence-wide Δ≥(log n/ε⁴)^{Θ((1/ε)log(1/ε))}.
A w.h.p. amortized bound for polynomial update sequences is an alternative; main figure uses expected worst-case.
sources.qualifier: No constant-degree guarantee, no absent recourse claim.

theorems: Deterministic, initially empty graph, fully current-Δ_t/current-α_t adaptive palette Δ_t+(4+ε)α_t.
O(log⁶n/ε⁶) amortized update time and O(log⁴n/ε⁵) amortized recourse.
sources.qualifier: Not replaced with the faster warmup requiring known fixed Δ and α.

sources.evidence: Official SWAT 2024 PDF, Theorem 14 printed p.20:14; Table 2; independent audit by cc_lca
theorems: Deterministic amortized insertion O(log n log α_max log Δ_max), deletion O(log²n log α_max log α log Δ_max).
Each edge uv uses a color at most max{deg_t(u),deg_t(v)}+O(α_t).
qualifiers: α_max and Δ_max are sequence maxima; use log⁺x=max{1,log x} in the display.
Theorem 9's faster known-fixed-bound guarantee has a different palette contract and is not substituted.

sources.evidence: Theorem 1.2, §§7.1–7.2; independent rounding audit by cc_lca
theorems: 2^{Õ_{log(1/ε)}(√log n)} deterministic amortized time, no high-degree promise, palette current-degree adaptive.
§7.1 ceiling convention handles low degree: Δ_max+1≤⌈(1+ε)Δ_max⌉.
qualifiers: Subpolynomial in n for ε⁻¹≤2^{O(log^0.49 n)}; not a uniform n-only exponent.
Intermediate splitter recourse in Theorem 1.4 is not the final edge-coloring recourse.

limitedEvidence: Two historical time records use explicit primary-abstract verification labels. No extra adversary regime or recourse was inferred.
